# The Harvest Theory

A premium food and wellness house from India — botanical beverages, teas, matcha, coffee and traditional nutritional foods, formulated around a simple philosophy: the right ingredients, grown the right way, harvested at the right time, brought together with purpose. Known in the brand's words as "Turning Exotics to Staples".

## Pages

- Home — the brand's philosophy ("There is a theory behind every harvest") and an overview of the collection.
- Products — 13 products across botanical beverages, teas and infusions, matcha, coffee and traditional nutritional foods, each with ingredients, preparation, tasting notes, pack size and price.
- Gift Assortments — curated seasonal tea boxes (Sacred Spring, Nexus) and tin gift-set configurations (Pink Symphony Assortment, Birds and Bees Collection, A Ballad in Blue).
- Our Approach — the brand's four pillars: selection and sourcing, formulation, testing and manufacturing, ritual and format.
- Our Story / Our Theory — the brand's origin and its theory of nourishment.
- Contact — enquiry types including product orders, retail/distributor and export enquiries.

## The Harvest Journal (editorial)

- Lopchu: a cup with a sense of place — a provenance story on the Lopchu tea estate in Darjeeling: altitude, China bushes, muscatel character and India's first Geographical Indication.
- Blue Pea: the flower that changes the colour of your cup — butterfly pea flower tea, its anthocyanin (ternatin) pigments and the chemistry behind the violet shift with lemon.
- Why chamomile became the tea of slowing down — the documented history of chamomile, its traditional evening association, and its classic pairing with lavender.
- Hibiscus: tart, crimson and unmistakable — hibiscus across cultures (agua de jamaica, karkadé, sorrel, bissap) and why cranberry pairs with it.
- There is more to mint tea than mint — menthol's cooling effect via the TRPM8 cold-sensing channel, lemongrass's citral aroma, and brewing herbal infusions.
- What exactly are you drinking when you drink a flower? — a field guide to floral infusions: where colour, aroma and flavour come from, and how to steep them.

The Journal focuses on ingredients, sensory characteristics, culture, provenance and ritual. It deliberately does not make therapeutic or health claims; relevant articles include a Sources & further reading list.
